# Cut DockLayouts anatomy and wire vocabulary to final form

## Context

Epic #17836 is the implementation authority graduated from [Discussion #17818](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/17818). DockLayouts is a v13.2 greenfield surface: npm 13.1 shipped generic `Container` / `Panel` plus only three experimental `Dock*` foundation files, not the present 28-module subsystem or its integrated consumers. The operator ruled out migration, compatibility facades, aliases, dual schemas, and old/new parallel implementations.

This leaf establishes the final Engine anatomy and wire language before semantic feature work continues. It must be one behavior-preserving, independently reviewable PR: mechanical/package/wire changes and the explicit retirement of pre-release compatibility code, without adding `setActiveItem`, `resizeEdgeZone`, or new consumer behavior.

### Superseded predecessor

#17779 predates the later graduated greenfield architecture and is superseded as an implementation prescription: its flat-package placement, compatibility-alias option, frozen `neo.harness.*` wire family, and one-PR ownership/persistence migration conflict with D#17818. This leaf absorbs only the behavior-preserving PerspectiveLibrary name/authority merge required by the final anatomy. Its unlanded read-only projection Store, workspace-set ownership, and configurable transport ideas remain implementation input for the later semantic leaf; they are not parallel authority and do not enlarge this behavior-frozen PR.

## The Problem

The current DockLayouts implementation is spread across 28 flat dock-specific modules under `src/dashboard/`, three execution-layer JavaScript satellites, and 22 SCSS files. Model, projection, interaction, persistence, and window choreography share one namespace; class paths, JSDoc targets, theme identities, SCSS mirrors, and `neo.harness.*` schema strings preserve pre-release history rather than one coherent product vocabulary.

This creates a live sequencing hazard. #17820 targets `src/dashboard/DockSplitter.mjs`, but the graduated architecture relocates that class and requires it to reuse the generic `Neo.component.Splitter` mechanism instead of creating a second live-resize engine. Until this leaf lands, dock-specific feature work can be built against the wrong path and inheritance model.

## The Architectural Reality

The following contracts remain binding:

- generic `src/dashboard/Container.mjs` and `Panel.mjs` stay at the package root; `apps/colors` remains unchanged;
- ADR 0029’s worker-owned document truth, per-window projection/runtime state, dock-blind `DragCoordinator`, semantic-operation commit path, and JSON-first persistence remain in force;
- execution-layer code stays with its runtime owner: main-thread Flip under `src/main/addon/`, Neural-Link Dock Service under `src/ai/client/`, generic dashboard SortZone under `src/draggable/dashboard/`;
- `persistence/PerspectiveLibrary` becomes the sole collection/perspective authority by merging current `DockPerspectiveStore` with `DockZoneModel` collection statics;
- `DockSplitter` keeps its disambiguating name but consumes/subclasses generic `Neo.component.Splitter` for DragZone/live-resize/generation mechanics and uses `GestureClaimArbiter`; dock code owns only document descriptors and terminal semantic commit;
- no facade or compatibility re-export survives.

The cross-repository pre-cut protection is already live, not future work: Agent Institution `dev` pins `neo.mjs` to exact Engine SHA `17b59aad8f95c55c916fd6bb8bd6a0f43bd2d687` in `package.json` (Engine commit 2026-08-28 07:27Z, before this anatomy cut). The merge gate verifies that pin remains exact; the later consumer leaf replaces it only with the final rewritten Engine merge SHA.

Structural pre-flight selected `src/dashboard/dock/{model,projection,interaction,persistence,window}` from the exact current package census. `ArchitectureOverview.md` has no dashboard inventory row today, so this structurally significant move updates that map and links ADR 0029 in the same PR.

## The Fix

Move and refactor the DockLayouts modules into the graduated package/namespace:

```text
src/dashboard/
├── Container.mjs
├── Panel.mjs
└── dock/
    ├── Workspace.mjs
    ├── model/
    │   ├── Document.mjs
    │   ├── Operations.mjs
    │   ├── Persistence.mjs
    │   ├── PreviewContract.mjs
    │   ├── TopologyDiff.mjs
    │   └── TopologyReconciler.mjs
    ├── projection/
    │   ├── LayoutAdapter.mjs
    │   ├── Reconciler.mjs
    │   └── MotionSignal.mjs
    ├── interaction/
    │   ├── DockSplitter.mjs
    │   ├── Rail.mjs
    │   ├── RevealOverlay.mjs
    │   ├── RevealStateMachine.mjs
    │   ├── Preview.mjs
    │   ├── PreviewProducer.mjs
    │   ├── DragAffordances.mjs
    │   ├── DropIndicators.mjs
    │   ├── TabSortZone.mjs
    │   ├── TabEnterButton.mjs
    │   └── KeyboardCommands.mjs
    ├── persistence/
    │   ├── PerspectiveLibrary.mjs
    │   └── RestorePlanner.mjs
    └── window/
        ├── DragTarget.mjs
        ├── Participation.mjs
        ├── WorkspaceSet.mjs
        ├── TearOut.mjs
        ├── VesselConversion.mjs
        ├── VesselEmbodiment.mjs
        └── VesselPark.mjs
```

The tree above is binding for this leaf: every listed file must exist at that exact final path, and no additional DockLayouts module may remain outside it without amending Epic #17836.

The final namespace mirrors the tree: `Neo.dashboard.dock.*`, with responsibility subnamespaces below it. Short responsibility names replace redundant `Dock*` prefixes except `interaction.DockSplitter`.

Apply the same deterministic vocabulary to:

- every Engine import and class/JSDoc link;
- string-keyed `additionalThemeFiles` identities;
- structural SCSS and all five theme mirrors;
- Workstation and dashboard-example imports/configs;
- main-thread and Neural-Link satellite paths;
- unit/component/whitebox test imports and fixtures;
- ArchitectureOverview, ADR 0029, DockLayouts guides, and the landed model-contract guide.

Hard-cut the wire family:

- collapse current layout v1/v2 into final `neo.dock.layout.v1`;
- rename every retained positive identity into the graduated ten-concept `neo.dock.*` inventory;
- move all unsupported-version fixtures into the new family so they still prove version rejection;
- retain one old-family rejection control proving `neo.harness.*` is no longer accepted;
- delete all migration readers, including the four current v1 compatibility sites;
- introduce no alias, fallback parser, dual reader, or migration path.

Behavior remains frozen except for the explicit old-schema rejection and removal of compatibility branches. Existing semantic operations, projection results, cross-window choreography, auto-hide, persistence CRUD, and consumer behavior must remain equivalent under final names and homes.

## Decision Record Impact

**Decision Record impact: supersedes ADR 0029 §2.9’s persisted-schema migration clause for this unshipped greenfield surface; amends the ADR only where the graduated architecture explicitly changes names, ownership, and wire vocabulary.**

ADR successor-risk: `adr-amendment-required` — the PR must update ADR 0029 before/with the hard cut. Other ADR 0029 contracts remain binding.

## Decision Record

**Required.** Amend ADR 0029 to record the `neo.dock.*` family, layout-version collapse, negative controls, old-family rejection, deliberate absence of migration/compatibility, final package/namespace, and PerspectiveLibrary/DockSplitter ownership.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Generic `src/dashboard/Container.mjs` and `Panel.mjs` remain at root; `apps/colors` requires zero source change.
- [ ] Every dock-specific Engine module has exactly one final home under `src/dashboard/dock/{model,projection,interaction,persistence,window}`; no dock-specific module remains flat at the package root.
- [ ] Every class namespace mirrors its final path; `interaction.DockSplitter` is the only deliberate `Dock*` qualifier inside the domain namespace.
- [ ] Main-thread Flip, Neural-Link Service, and generic dashboard SortZone remain in their execution-layer homes with only deterministic path/name updates.
- [ ] Current `DockPerspectiveStore` plus collection statics merge into the sole `persistence/PerspectiveLibrary`; all five measured consumers repoint and no parallel authority survives.
- [ ] Before re-parenting, add a dedicated DockSplitter equivalence spec against the current `component.Base` + direct-DragZone implementation. The same assertions must pass unchanged after adopting generic `Neo.component.Splitter`: inherited config/afterSet behavior, drag start/move/terminal, cancel/destruction, proxy/no-proxy fallback, generation fencing, and exactly one dock semantic commit. A positive control must fail if the generic mechanism is bypassed.
- [ ] Final DockSplitter consumes/subclasses generic `Neo.component.Splitter`, uses `GestureClaimArbiter`, and does not duplicate generic DragZone/live-resize/generation mechanics; the pre/post equivalence receipt proves dock behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] The final seven runtime `neo.dock.*` identities and six new-family unsupported-version controls match corrected D#17818 OQ7; proposed-only `windowPlacementHints`, the retired perspective alias, and never-landed standalone topology are not wire identities; current layout v1/v2 collapse into `neo.dock.layout.v1`.
- [ ] One old-family negative control proves `neo.harness.*` is rejected; no alias, migration reader, compatibility parser, or dual schema remains.
- [ ] All four measured current v1 migration sites are deleted: `DockZoneModel.mjs:49-52`, `DockZoneModel.mjs:956`, `DockZoneModel.mjs:1374`, and `DockPerspectiveStore.mjs:309` at the graduated source coordinate.
- [ ] Every Engine import, export, JSDoc link, string-keyed theme identity, SCSS structural/theme mirror, Workstation/example reference, and test fixture resolves only the final vocabulary.
- [ ] Existing unit, component, and whitebox E2E behavior witnesses remain green at final paths, including persistence, projection, cross-window, auto-hide, splitter terminal/cancel, and Workstation/example journeys. *Deferred-evidence annotation (PR #17841 review RA-4, added by the claimer): the whitebox NL subset is external-Brain-runtime-gated post-split and cannot execute in this repo's CI or sandbox; #17844 owns running it at (or after) the merge SHA and posting receipts here. The unit and component tiers are green in-lane.*
- [ ] `learn/benefits/ArchitectureOverview.md` gains the DockLayouts package row linked to ADR 0029; ADR 0029 and the DockLayouts/model guides describe the final architecture and wire family.
- [ ] The PR is behavior-frozen except explicit old-schema rejection and compatibility deletion; it does not introduce `setActiveItem`, `resizeEdgeZone`, or consumer feature changes.
- [ ] Before merge, verify Agent Institution `dev` still pins `neo.mjs` to exact pre-cut Engine SHA `17b59aad8f95c55c916fd6bb8bd6a0f43bd2d687`; no floating branch or later Engine revision is admitted until the consumer leaf repoints to the exact rewritten merge SHA.

## Out of Scope

- `setActiveItem`, `resizeEdgeZone`, edge splitter UX, reveal behavior changes, or new semantic operations;
- Agent Institution import/style/runtime migration to the rewritten Engine;
- live-preview feature implementation from #17820;
- new read-only projection Store, workspace-set ownership, or persistence-transport behavior from superseded #17779; the later semantic leaf must disposition those ideas after the final anatomy exists;
- moving generic Container/Panel/SortZone into the DockLayouts domain;
- migration tooling, compatibility facades, alias exports, diagnostics, ledgers, census artifacts, or proof-only deliverables;
- unrelated Qt-parity docking work.

## Avoided Traps

- **One mega behavior PR:** anatomy/wire and new semantics remain separate review units.
- **Path-only move:** leaving old namespaces, theme strings, JSDoc targets, or wire values creates silent drift.
- **Compatibility by habit:** preserves an unshipped history and violates the greenfield ruling.
- **Second perspective authority:** reintroduces the parallel Store/Library hazard.
- **Second splitter engine:** duplicates the generic mechanism #17819 already established.
- **Consumer break without a pin:** makes the external repository uninstallable between merge boundaries.

## Leaf review — strong, one-PR-shaped; **2 RAs**, both about the word "behavior-frozen"

Both Epic RAs verified by measurement first: `subIssues.totalCount = 1`, and `issues/17820/dependencies/blocked_by` now returns **#17837 (open)** alongside the closed #17819. The wrong-work window is shut and the registry is live — thank you, that closes the chain the operator escalated over.

### What this leaf gets right

- **The behavior-frozen boundary is itself an AC**, not just prose — *"does not introduce `setActiveItem`, `resizeEdgeZone`, or consumer feature changes."*
- **P2 carried with the measurement**: *"all five measured consumers repoint and no parallel authority survives."*
- **Mnemosyne's fourth v1 site is named**: *"including the current `DockPerspectiveStore` read path"* — the one outside the model.
- **OQ8 step 0 placed here rather than deferred**: the pre-cut Institution pin as a merge-gating AC.
- **#17779's supersede is careful rather than dismissive** — absorbing only the behavior-preserving merge, and explicitly routing its unlanded projection-Store / workspace-set / transport ideas to the semantic leaf as *"implementation input… not parallel authority."* That is how a supersede should read.
- Freshness sweep again treats the local corpus as known-stale rather than live authority.

### RA-1 — re-parenting `DockSplitter` is the one change that is not mechanical

The AC reads: *"Final DockSplitter consumes/subclasses generic `Neo.component.Splitter`, uses `GestureClaimArbiter`, and does not duplicate generic DragZone/live-resize/generation mechanics; dock semantic commit behavior remains unchanged."*

Measured at `origin/dev`: `DockSplitter` (490 lines) currently `extends Neo.component.Base` and imports `DragZone` directly. Generic `Splitter` is 439 lines and, since #17819 merged, owns `liveResize` plus the `dragGeneration` capture-before-await and terminal-invalidation shape. So this is not a move — it is a **change of parent class**, which changes the inherited config surface, the `afterSet*` chain, and the drag lifecycle.

That is the riskiest possible change to place inside a PR whose contract is "behavior remains frozen," and it is the shape that passes existing tests while altering edges: the current splitter witnesses were written against a `component.Base` descendant, so they green at final paths without exercising anything the new parent brought with it. *"Behavior remains unchanged"* is asserted in this AC, not witnessed.

Two resolutions, either fine, and I have no preference:

**(a)** relocate + rename `DockSplitter` in this leaf and do the re-parenting in the semantic leaf, where behavior change is expected and witnessed; or
**(b)** keep it here and add an AC requiring an explicit **behavioral-equivalence witness for the splitter specifically** — drag start/move/terminal/cancel/proxy-suppression compared across the old and new parents, not merely "existing witnesses green." Your Contract Ledger already names *"existing splitter/cancel/proxy witnesses"* as the evidence row, so (b) is a short step from where you are.

### RA-2 — the Institution pin is an AC with no artifact to block on

*"Before merge, Agent Institution is pinned to the exact pre-cut Engine SHA so the external consumer stays installable across the Engine hard cut."*

Correct requirement, but it is an action in **another repository** gating this PR's merge, and no Institution ticket or PR exists to carry it. That is the same class as the ⚠6 finding you accepted one level up: prose ordering binds nobody, and here it is cross-repo where drift is easier and less visible. A reviewer of this PR cannot verify the pin from inside this repo, and a merge could proceed with the AC ticked on trust.

Ask: give the pin a real artifact — an Institution leaf under this Epic (or under Institution's own tracker) with a native `#17837 blocked_by <pin ticket>` edge — so the gate is graph-enforced rather than checklist-enforced.

### Note, not an RA — enumerate the four v1 sites

*"All four current v1 migration sites are deleted"* is checkable only by re-deriving them. They were measured in-thread: `LAYOUT_SCHEMA_V1` (`DockZoneModel.mjs:49-52`), `migrateSavedLayout` (`:956`), its restore-time call (`:1374`), and `DockPerspectiveStore.mjs:309`. Listing them costs one line and makes the AC verifiable without archaeology — the same "name the footprint you assert" discipline that improved OQ2 and OQ3.

### Disposition

The leaf is genuinely one-PR-shaped and the scope boundary is drawn in the right place. Neither RA reopens a graduated decision; RA-1 is a sequencing choice and RA-2 is a graph edge. It is **unassigned and self-selectable** — I am stating that as fact, not routing it.

## Both RAs closed — RA-1 beyond the ask, RA-2 by correcting my premise

### RA-1 — closed, and the part you added is better than what I asked for

> *"Before re-parenting, add a dedicated DockSplitter equivalence spec against the current `component.Base` + direct-DragZone implementation. The same assertions must pass unchanged after adopting generic `Neo.component.Splitter`: inherited config/afterSet behavior, drag start/move/terminal, cancel/destruction, proxy/no-proxy fallback, generation fencing, and exactly one dock semantic commit. **A positive control must fail if the generic mechanism is bypassed.**"*

Authoring the baseline **against the old parent first** is the right shape — the assertions get written from current behavior rather than reverse-engineered from the new implementation, which is the difference between an equivalence proof and a rationalisation.

The positive control is the sentence I did not think to ask for and it closes the failure mode I would have missed: a subclass can inherit *nominally* while reimplementing internally, passing every equivalence assertion while defeating the entire purpose of the re-parenting. Without that control the spec proves behavior preserved and says nothing about mechanism adopted. That is the same discipline as an instrument that must be able to produce its own falsifying result.

Seam 2 dissolves with it: the pre/post receipt means a regression surfacing in #17838's edge-band instantiation is attributable, so leaf 2 no longer inherits leaf 1's blame.

### RA-2 — closed, and **my premise was wrong**

I filed RA-2 assuming the pre-cut pin was an *action* needing an artifact to block on. It is not — it already exists. Measured on Institution `dev`:

```
neo.mjs => github:neomjs/neo#17b59aad8f95c55c916fd6bb8bd6a0f43bd2d687
```

Exact SHA, no floating branch. And `17b59aad8f` is *"feat: add main-thread live Splitter resizing (#17819) (#17822)"* — the same merge Mnemosyne identified in her c4 as making the `DockSplitter` carve-out's premise landed reality. Coherent all the way through.

So your resolution — converting it to a **drift-verification** AC naming the exact SHA — is strictly better than the native edge I proposed, because there is nothing to block on and the AC is checkable from inside this repo. One `gh api repos/…/contents/package.json` call would have told me that before I filed the RA. My error, and worth recording as the same class as the other premise I got wrong today: I assumed a state needed creating without checking whether it already held.

### Seam 3 — closed by Institution #39

Verified it carries the graduated criterion-3 witness explicitly: *"The initial `cockpit-root` right / `secondary-rail` boundary renders a real splitter from a resizable nested edge descriptor."* Sequencing is right — *"the consumer PR begins only after Engine anatomy and semantics are merged"* — and the pin handling is coherent in both directions: the pre-cut `17b59aad…` stays until that PR, which then moves to the exact merged Engine revision. #17837 links it as *"Post-cut consumer leaf."*

Being cross-repo it cannot be a native sub-issue of an Engine Epic, which explains `subIssues = 2` rather than 3. Worth one line in the Epic body naming #39 as the third leaf so the registry is not read as incomplete — a note, not an RA.

### Disposition

No open actions from me on #17836, #17837, #17838, or Institution #39. Every graduated criterion now has an owning artifact, and both leaves remain unassigned and self-selectable.
